Morgan — thanks for the signal and the file. Appreciate the clarity on the commit shape. A few quick points: 

- Step-down: our standard safety net is a 60-day adjustment window with a tiered prorate (we can map this to a clear step-down schedule). For >30% drop we normally apply a 45–60 day notice with a one-time grace credit to smooth the first billing cycle. I can draft exact language.
- Onboarding discount: 18–20% is larger than standard for this packaging; we typically do 10–15% tied to a 12-month committed usage. That said, for enterprise pilots we have flexibility if we get a signed MAA + a firm 12-month commit and an internal SLA addendum.

I'm looping Lauren to validate margin impact and to propose a concrete counter (I can share a redline MAA after internal alignment). If you want to lock week-of-Nov 8 for signature, we can prepare the MAA + SOW.

Would you prefer I send a short concessions table (banded discounts by ARR/commit size) or a single offer with a fixed % and step-down language?

On copy: attaching a preliminary MAA sketch.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Ben / Lauren — forwarding Epoch's ask. Key asks: 18–20% onboarding discount (12-mo), and clear step-down behavior for >30% QoQ drop. Morgan asked for a fast turnaround — they're willing to sign W/C Nov 8.

My thoughts: if we do a banded concession table we preserve margin and make room for legal-friendly step-down language. Options I want your take on:

1) Conservative: 12% one-time onboarding credit + 30-day grace credit on first billing cycle; step-down prorate over 60 days.
2) Aggressive: 18% off first 12 months, but requires a minimum ARR threshold and a non-refundable onboarding fee to cover ramp costs.
3) Hybrid: 15% off first 9 months + a 1-month free sandbox credit; step-down with 45-day notice.

Lauren: what's the margin hit on option 2 at the ARR they're projecting (attached sheet)? Ben: can we preserve a limited-seat-rollback clause to protect us if they underutilize?

Notes: keep public pricing guardrails in the offer so we can revert if utilization drifts. I attached the MAA_draft_v1 and their sku split.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Packaging signal for Nov commit — discount ask (concrete counter)

Morgan — thanks for the clear signal and apologies for the slightly long turnaround. We discussed internally and here's a concise counter that balances your request and our guardrails: 

Offer (counter):
- Commitment: 12-month MAA tied to committed monthly throughput (outline in attached sku split).
- Onboarding concession: 15% credit applied across the first 9 billing months. Credit is applied monthly as an invoice credit (not a cash rebate).
- Step-down policy: if usage drops >30% QoQ, we allow a one-time step-down with 45 days' notice and a prorated adjustment; to protect baseline economics, a one-time stabilization credit is applied to the customer (equivalent to 1 month at the post-discount effective rate).
- Non-refundable onboarding fee: $10k (covers dedicated kickoff engineering and priority queueing). Fee waived if contract signed by Nov 12.

Additional items:
- We'll include a clause that allows reversion to published list prices if utilization falls below 50% of committed throughput for two consecutive months.
- SLA & SLO addendum: standard Dedicated uptime SLA; we'll include a 14-day remediation window for outages that materially affect throughput.

If that looks reasonable from your side we can: (1) publish an MAA redline this afternoon, (2) share a DocuSign link for signature, (3) schedule a 30-min onboarding kickoff upon signature.

DocuSign (proposed): https://app.docusign.com/link/EPOCH-453-offer
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/EPOCH-453

LMK and we'll fast-track legal.

—Ben
